newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges steady to weaker.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges steady to weaker.

text.p: NWE prompt high sulphur fuel oil prices fell again on Tuesday but early February barrels were worth slightly more after crude oil futures firmed, traders said.

High sulphur barges loading this month traded at $91 fob ARA, amid a continued lack of bunker demand, but prices for early February were pegged $3 or so higher. February swaps traded at $96.25 fob ARA.
High sulphur cargoes were little changed. A utility player said he saw an offer in the morning at $95.50 cif NWE, for an ARA-origin piece loading in mid to late February.
Dealers said they thought a trader had bought as much as 50,000 tonnes of U.S. origin material to cover commitments into an Irish utility, but this was not confirmed.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady to firmer with crude.
A refiner in Scandinavia on Monday sold a low sulphur cargo, loading around mid February, to an affiliate in Italy. The refiner in Italy still has a requirement for high sulphur ENEL-quality barrels.
Other offers of low sulphur fuel oil were seen out of Scandinavia and the U.K., but the market is not seen as long now as last week.
